title: Where should 2, 3 and 5 go to make the biggest multiplication?
description: The digits two, three and five fill a frame of two boxes times one box. The six ways are listed, the larger number is kept from each pair, and place value shows which of the last two wins. Keeko then doubts the plan of making the biggest two digit number first.
teaching_notes: One idea: the one digit multiplier works on both digits of the other number, so the largest digit is the multiplier and the other two go in decreasing order. Watch for students who build the biggest two digit number first and leave the smallest digit to multiply.

source: Place the digits 2, 3 and 5 to make the largest two digit by
video_script.why: The child sees that listing the ways, keeping the larger of each pair and comparing by place value finds the largest multiplication answer.
video_script.substitution: Fill the digits 2, 3 and 5 in two boxes times one box, group the six ways by multiplier, keep the larger number of each pair, and compare by expanding.
video_script.anchor: the frame of two boxes, a times sign and one box, with the digits 2, 3 and 5 to place
video_script.wrong_answer: make the biggest two digit number first
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko makes the largest two digit number first, fifty three, and leaves the smallest digit to multiply, so the answer stays small.
video_script.payoff_line: The largest answer is thirty two times five, which is one hundred sixty

final_answer.spoken: thirty two times five, which is one hundred sixty

maths_rules: pairs by multiplier: 35 × 2 and 53 × 2; 25 × 3 and 52 × 3; 23 × 5 and 32 × 5
keep the larger number of each pair: 53 × 2, 52 × 3, 32 × 5
video_script.design: One idea: the largest digit is the multiplier. The frame and the six ways stay on the board all video. Keeko's doubt is to make the biggest two digit number first.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='cards'/>It gives you the digits two, three and five.
<bookmark mark='frame'/>They go into a frame with two boxes, the times sign and one box.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Each digit is used once. Where should each digit go to make the multiplication answer as large as possible?

narration: <bookmark mark='six'/>Any digit can be the multiplier, and the other two can swap places. That gives six ways.
<bookmark mark='pair'/>Group the ways that have the same multiplier into pairs.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>In each pair, the larger two digit number gives the larger answer.

marks.given: the digits and the frame are written on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the digits two, three and five, each used once. They fill a two digit number times a one digit number.

beats.on_screen: To find: the largest multiplication answer

marks.find: the words largest multiplication answer are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the largest multiplication answer.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: keep the larger number of each pair: 53 × 2, 52 × 3, 32 × 5

marks.keep: the three larger ways stay and the other three fade

narration: <bookmark mark='keep'/>Step one, keep the larger two digit number from each pair, because the same multiplier works on it.
<bookmark mark='list'/>Three ways are left, fifty three times two, fifty two times three, and thirty two times five.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, compare the first two. Fifty three times two is one hundred six.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Fifty two times three is one hundred fifty six, which is larger.
<bookmark mark='out'/>Fifty three times two is out.

marks.expand: both products are expanded by place value
marks.same: the two 150s are boxed as equal
marks.rest: 6 and 10 light up, and 10 is larger

beats.colours: the equal parts in one colour, the last parts in two
narration: <bookmark mark='expand'/>Step three, split each one by place value. Fifty two times three is five times ten times three, plus two times three.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Thirty two times five is three times ten times five, plus two times five. Both first parts are one hundred fifty.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>The second parts are six and ten, and ten is larger.

marks.rule: the largest digit 5 is marked as the multiplier

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The largest answer is thirty two times five, which is one hundred sixty.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The largest digit is the multiplier, and the other two digits go in decreasing order.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 53 × 2; 106 appears under it and is struck out beside 160

marks.fix: the multiplier 5 glows as reaching both digits of 32

beats.colours: the wrong way in the warning colour
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks we should make the biggest two digit number first, fifty three, and multiply it by two.
<bookmark mark='test'/>But that gives only one hundred six, far below one hundred sixty.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The multiplier works on both digits, so the largest digit belongs there.
